initial_prompt: I've been feeling really lonely lately. None of my friends seem to have time for me anymore.

messages.content: I've been feeling really lonely lately. None of my friends seem to have time for me anymore.

That sounds really painful. Loneliness has a way of making everything feel heavier.

I'm curious what's actually happening here - because "friends don't have time for me" can mean a few different things:

- They're genuinely busier (life phases shift - new jobs, relationships, kids)
- The friendship has drifted and neither side is investing much
- You're reaching out and getting turned down
- You're not reaching out because you assume they're too busy
- Something in the dynamic has changed that you're sensing but can't quite name

Do you know which of these feels closest? Because they'd call for pretty different responses.

Also - when you say "none" of your friends, is that literally true, or does it feel that way right now? Sometimes loneliness distorts our perception so that a few disappointing interactions feel like a total pattern.

I'm not asking to challenge you - I just want to understand what you're actually facing before jumping to advice that might miss the mark.

metadata.context: Testing v3: Emotional vulnerability - does warmth come through?
